rows.text: Conservation runs on two strategies. rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
In-situ conservation protects a species in the place where it already lives, so its partners and its climate stay with it.
National parks, wildlife reserves, conservation areas and buffer zones are the in-situ tools. Chitwan is the first national park. Annapurna is a conservation area where villages remain.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **National park vs conservation area:** park = strict state protection, no settlement; conservation area = community-managed sustainable use (Annapurna, ACAP).  ·  **Genebank vs botanical garden:** genebank stores dormant seeds/cryo material; a garden grows living labelled plants.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short answer (2m):** What is a biodiversity hotspot? **Answer.** A region with **exceptionally high endemic species richness undergoing severe habitat loss** — the two criteria together. Nepal falls inside the **Himalaya hotspot**. Hotspots are where in-situ conservation investment buys the most species saved per rupee.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **The evolution argument:** only in-situ conservation lets species keep adapting to a changing world — ex-situ buys time, in-situ buys the future.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: In-situ: species in habitat — national parks (Chitwan 1973, Shey-Phoksundo largest), wildlife reserves (Koshi Tappu — arna), conservation areas (Annapurna ACAP), hunting reserve (Dhorpatan), Ramsar wetlands, Himalaya hotspot.  ·  Ex-situ: outside habitat — botanical garden (Godawari), zoo (Central Zoo Jawalakhel), seed bank (Khumaltar genebank), tissue culture, cryopreservation, captive breeding (gharial, vulture).  ·  In-situ preserves evolution; ex-situ pauses it.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Nepal doubled its tiger population between 2009 and 2022 — one of the few countries to meet the TX2 goal, entirely through in-situ conservation.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Keeping Species Alive Conservation biology distinguishes two grand strategies: **in-situ** conservation protects species where they live; **ex-situ** conservation protects them elsewhere — in gardens, banks and cages. Nepal, a biodiversity hotspot with 2% of the world's flowering plants and flagship megafauna, uses both.  ·  ## 2.
